name: Scandinavian — Qd6 Variation
description: The Qd6 Scandinavian keeps the queen more central than Qa5. After 3...Qd6, Black accepts a slight space disadvantage — White gains c4 — in exchange for a solid, flexible position. The critical light bishop comes out to g4 before ...e6 locks it in, then trades on f3 to give White a doubled-pawn structure. Black builds with ...e6, ...Be7, and ...O-O for a principled, sound counterplay.

lines.name: Scandinavian — Qd6 Variation
lines.description: After 3...Qd6, White plays Nf3 and d4 for rapid central development. Black responds 4...Nf6 (developing with tempo), 5...Bg4 (the critical bishop MUST come out before ...e6), 6...Bxf3 (trading the bishop for the knight, giving White doubled pawns), 7...e6, 8...Be7. Both sides complete development. White's Qf3 and Bd3 create long-term central pressure; Black's solid pawn chain supports queenside counterplay.
